expectations.text: The reply separates the temporary part of the drop from the structural part, using evidence such as the order book, customer forecasts or the quotes pipeline, and says the answer depends on that split.
expectations.evidence: It separates the two ('You have two different problems, not one. One customer's cut may be cyclical; the other's move to electric drivetrains is structural') and says harder measures come 'only if the numbers prove earlier ones cannot close the gap'. But it names no evidence for the split. The roadmap simply labels Customer A 'volume dip, likely to return' and says to 'Quantify the exact Euro gap... by separating Customer A's temporary dip from Customer B's permanent loss', without asking for the order book, a customer volume outlook or the quotes pipeline. That is an assumed split, not an evidence-tested one.

expectations.text: The reply matches the tool to the cause: short-time work or reduced hours only for the part that will pass, with its conditions flagged (such as works council agreement where there is one, or the maximum duration), and a real plan for the structural part, such as new sectors or customers, products, redeployment or retraining.
expectations.evidence: Reply: 'Use Kurzarbeit for the temporary dip, and pivot for the permanent one... (with Betriebsrat agreement if you have one; note the 24-month maximum runs until 31 December 2026 and reverts to 12 months on 1 January 2027 unless extended)', plus 'deploy your sales and engineering leads to win non-ICE work—EV/battery tooling, energy, medical, defence subcontracting, and paid service/retrofits'. The roadmap table maps right and wrong tools per problem, with redeployment, reskilling and Altersteilzeit for the structural part.

expectations.text: The reply gives the bank what it needs in its own terms: a cash-flow forecast, covenant headroom, scenarios and the actions each scenario would trigger, rather than only a headcount number.
expectations.evidence: Roadmap: 'Build a 13-week rolling cash-flow forecast and a 2027 P&L under three demand scenarios (base, downside, severe)'. The bank pack has a '13-week cash-flow & 2027–2028 liquidity bridge: Showing you can service debt and stay inside the credit line', a 'Two-track capacity plan' (Kurzarbeit for the dip, structural adjustment 'only if numbers require it'), and 'Governance & milestones: Monthly KPIs' tracking 'liquidity headroom'. Scenarios are not explicitly mapped to actions, but the package is in the bank's terms.

expectations.text: The reply works the levers that don't cost jobs first (for example spend, pricing, working capital or inventory) and puts the owner first, such as the owner's own draw or dividend, before jobs.
expectations.evidence: Reply step 1: 'Freeze non-essential capex and external hiring, and launch a working-capital sprint (overdue receivables, excess WIP/inventory, vendor terms)'. Step 2: 'Cut your own management pay, bonuses, perks, and family drawings first'. The roadmap orders options from working capital and pricing through owner sacrifice before hours, voluntary exits and involuntary cuts.

expectations.text: The reply protects the apprentices and scarce skills, and if some reductions remain, plans them once and decently: works council, German legal steps such as social selection or mass-dismissal notification, and counsel, flagged as not legal advice.
expectations.evidence: 'Protect all 14 apprentices... (§22 BBiG)'. Skills: 'keeps skilled machinists ready for recovery', 'Risk of losing your best Facharbeiter'. Process: 'one clean, well-planned reduction—once, decently, with outplacement and coaching funded from day one of notice—not repeated rounds', Betriebsrat, §§111–112 BetrVG, §17 KSchG, Sozialauswahl, and '(Not legal advice—confirm your exact exposure with employment counsel this week.)'

expectations.text: The reply treats the family firm's long-term view and reputation as assets and answers the owner's values honestly: it neither promises that no job will ever go nor dismisses his grandfather's principle.
expectations.evidence: 'Your grandfather's rule—never laying anyone off—built the trust you are standing on today. You honour that legacy best not by pretending a permanent market shift isn't happening, but by exhausting every commercial, cash, and shared-hour lever before touching a single job.' The roadmap counts 'brand damage in Stuttgart' as a cost of cuts, and 'banks respect owners who share the pain' in a third-generation family business. It honours the principle without promising zero cuts.

factual_errors.evidence: One minor error: the §17 KSchG threshold is given as 'more than 10% (or >25 people)' (reply) and 'more than 10% or more than 25 employees' (roadmap). The statute is 10% (reaching it is enough) or more than 25. This doesn't matter at 45 people. Also overstated, but not counted: 'firing 45 people in Q4 2026 increases cash outflow in Q1 2027'. Severance is normally paid at exit, after the negotiations and notice periods. Correct: §§111–112 BetrVG, §1(3) KSchG criteria, §622 BGB 7 months, §22 BBiG, §87(1) no. 3 BetrVG, KuG 24→12 months, IAB 2026 warning.

skill_leak.evidence: No skill, reference-file or ladder/rung jargon (it has an options table 'Ordered from Least to Most Human Harm' but no ladder or rung wording).

owns_result.evidence: Leaders cut their pay first, but no leader says the responsibility for the outcome is leadership's.

best_insight.value: It proposes a monthly review, shared with leadership and employee representatives, that tracks cash metrics (liquidity headroom, non-ICE order intake, WIP days) alongside people metrics (sickness, voluntary turnover, training hours), so the bank and the workforce see the same scorecard.

suggestions.assertion: The reply gives the bank what it needs in its own terms: a cash-flow forecast, covenant headroom, scenarios and the actions each scenario would trigger, rather than only a headcount number.
suggestions.reason: The four bank elements are listed without 'such as', so it is unclear whether all are required. Several samples give a cash forecast and a clean trigger but never mention covenants or headroom, while others list scenarios and covenants with no scenario-to-action mapping. Say which elements are required.

suggestions.assertion: The reply protects the apprentices and scarce skills, and if some reductions remain, plans them once and decently: works council, German legal steps such as social selection or mass-dismissal notification, and counsel, flagged as not legal advice.
suggestions.reason: This bundles about seven checks (apprentices, scarce skills, once, works council, social selection or §17, counsel, not-legal-advice flag). One missing item, such as the word 'once' or a disclaimer, fails an otherwise excellent answer. Split it into 'protects apprentices and scarce skills' and 'plans any remaining cuts once, with legal steps and counsel'.

No assertion checks the German facts that drive the timing: Kurzarbeit's 24-month maximum falls back to 12 months on 1 January 2027, right before the February bank date, and dismissal savings land mid-2027 because of §17 KSchG, social-plan talks and notice periods of up to seven months. Most samples get these right; an assertion would catch the ones that are vague (G) or that overstate how much cash dismissals burn before February (D, I, J).

eval_feedback.overall: Solid and humane, with a useful bank pack and roadmap; it assumes which customer's drop is temporary instead of testing it against the order book or customer outlooks, and states the §17 threshold slightly wrong.
